text:
Two teams in a rough patch meet in Vancouver. The Flyers are on the second night of a back-to-back after losing 4-3 in overtime at Calgary, where Matt Coronato got the winner, and they're winless in three without Rasmus Ristolainen. The Canucks are 0-5-0 in their last five, outscored 22-12, and they're missing Filip Chytil. Elias Pettersson has taken his spot beside Jonathan Lekkeriмäki and Brock Boeser.

The numbers don't separate them. Both teams have taken 41% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) at five on five. Vancouver allows more per 60, 3.77 to Philadelphia's 3.48, and its penalty kill is the leakier one. Our model has PHI at 3.11 expected goals tonight and VAN at 2.94. In net, projected starter Joseph Woll is 3.86 goals saved above expected this season, while Leevi Meriläinen is at -2.33 and has struggled over his last five starts (.848).

Boeser is on a four-game point streak and is two points from 500 for his career. For Philadelphia, Matvei Michkov is at 56% for a point, though he spoke out publicly about his ice time this week. Our under-the-radar picks are both Flyers. Cole Knuble, a fourth-liner, has 2.3 expected goals in his last nine games, and Vancouver gives up the second-most expected goals per 60. Porter Martone, newly in the top six beside Michkov, sits at 46% for a point, above his season pace.
